guarantees.claim: When reset (rst_ni=0) is active, cfg_block is cleared to 0.
When hash_start_or_continue is asserted and not in reset, cfg_block is set to 1.
When hash_start_or_continue is not asserted and either reg_hash_done or reg_hash_stop is asserted (and not in reset), cfg_block is cleared to 0.
In all other non-reset cases (no set, no clear condition), cfg_block holds its previous value.

assumptions.claim: hash_start_or_continue is pulsed and deasserts after the start request is accepted; otherwise cfg_block will be forced to 1 constantly.
assumptions.cond: when hash_start_or_continue is used to start a hash operation
assumptions.risk: cfg_block stuck at 1, preventing the block from ever being cleared by done/stop, causing the design to believe a hash is always in progress.

assumptions.claim: reg_hash_done and reg_hash_stop are pulsed (deassert after a few cycles); if either stays high, it will permanently clear cfg_block, overriding any subsequent start.
assumptions.cond: normal operation after a hash completes or is stopped
assumptions.risk: cfg_block cannot be set again, blocking further hash operations until the signal deasserts.

assumptions.claim: The set condition (hash_start_or_continue) has higher priority than the clear condition (reg_hash_done/reg_hash_stop). The rest of the design must be tolerant to cfg_block becoming 1 even when done/stop are asserted simultaneously.
assumptions.cond: when hash_start_or_continue and (reg_hash_done or reg_hash_stop) are asserted in the same cycle
assumptions.risk: If downstream logic expects cfg_block to be cleared immediately on done/stop, a simultaneous start will cause a spurious active cycle, potentially leading to incorrect state propagation.

uncertain_points.claim: The priority of hash_start_or_continue over reg_hash_done/reg_hash_stop may be intentional; however, the specification does not clarify whether a new start should be allowed to override an in-progress done/stop condition.
uncertain_points.cond: when hash_start_or_continue and (reg_hash_done or reg_hash_stop) are true simultaneously
uncertain_points.risk: A start that coincides with a done/stop could create an unexpected state where the hash core begins a new operation while the previous one finishes, potentially causing data corruption or lost done notification.
